title: TLDR: Observability plan — KV-prefetch signals and dashboard UX notes
content:
TL;DR: put the minimal set of signals in front of oncall and product for the next rollout (quantized models, dedicated burst). Focus: KV-prefetch efficacy, TTFB attribution, dashboard micro-tiles for fast triage.

Summary goals:
- Ship a compact dashboard surface (6 micro-tiles) that answers: is it cold cache? is prefetch working? did model quantization change token-path latency? are errors creeping up?
- Define 6 primary metrics, precise derivations, and trace anchors for each.
- Sampling plan: severity-tiered trace capture to balance cost.
- Acceptance checklist for rollout: metric regressions within guardrails, end-to-end synthetic probe pass, and prefetched-hit-streak >= 95% for steady state.

Primary metric definitions (single-line derivations + notes):
1) ttfb-50-ms (string): median time-to-first-byte per request (end-user timestamp -> first token emitted). Window: 5m, agg: p50/p95. Notes: exclude synthetic probes; tag by model_variant and tenant.
2) kv-warmth-index (string): ratio(prefetch_hits / prefetch_attempts) per tenant over 1h. Value in [0,1]. Use moving-average(5m) for dashboards; keep raw histogram for investigation.
3) prefetch-efficacy-score (string): weighted_score = 0.6*kv-warmth-index + 0.4*(1 - cold_retry_rate). Purpose: single actionable number for operators.
4) kv-eviction-spike-count (string): count of eviction events where eviction_rate > 2x baseline within 5m. Baseline = rolling 24h median. Important for capacity-driven regressions.
5) token-path-latency-decomposition (string): stack of service-level increments: router_ms + batch_wait_ms + model_infer_ms + flush_ms. Each is a metric; store as separate series but decomposed on chart.
6) sampling-weighted-error-rate (string): error_count * sampling_inverse_weight / requests. Allows accurate error-rate estimation under sampling.

Trace span and annotation conventions (anchors to use in traces):
- span:request.router (attributes: tenant_id, route, model_variant, request_id)
- span:batch.wait (attributes: batch_id, requested_batch_size, actual_batch_size)
- span:model.exec (attributes: model_family, quantized=true/false, seq_len)
- annotations: kv_prefetch:attempt=true/false, kv_prefetch:hit=true/false, kv_prefetch:lat_ms=NN
Naming notes: always include customer_tenant as a tag; use short names for spans to keep storage down.

Dashboard UX: micro-tiles & drill flow:
- Tile 1: TTFB p50/p95 small sparkline + heatmap by region. Click -> session-level trace list filtered by kv_prefetch:false.
- Tile 2: Prefetch-efficacy score (big number) with trend. Click -> time-windowed cohort breakdown (model_variant, tenant).
- Tile 3: Eviction spike map (per pool) with anomaly markers. Click -> recent eviction traces + GC logs.
- Tile 4: Token path decomposition stacked bars (router, batching, model). Click -> compare quantized vs non-quantized model variants.
- Tile 5: Sampling-weighted-error-rate + top error signatures. Click -> example traces + prompt snippets (redact PII).
- Tile 6: Synthetic probe status (last run, delta from baseline). Click -> probe run details and canary toggles.

Investigation playbook (operator quick-steps):
1) Look at Tile 1 and 2. If TTFB p95 spikes and prefetch-efficacy drops -> suspect cold-cache / failed prefetch.
2) Jump to trace list using router span -> filter for kv_prefetch:attempt=true, kv_prefetch:hit=false. Inspect model.exec durations.
3) If batch_wait_ms is high and actual_batch_size << requested_batch_size -> routing or autoscaling issue.
4) If model.exec grows across both prefetched and non-prefetched -> model kernel or quantization regression. Check recent rollouts.
5) Use Tile 6 to validate synthetic probe vs user traffic divergence.

Sampling policy (cost vs fidelity):
- severity=high (errors, eviction spikes, prefetch failure) -> capture full traces (100%) for 10m window
- severity=medium (ttfb p95 > threshold) -> capture 25% for 30m
- baseline -> sparse sampling 0.5% + 1 trace per unique request_hash per hour for coverage
- keep sampled traces tagged with session_id and tenant; run nightly aggregation job to estimate unbiased metrics using sampling_inverse_weight.

Quick experiments (2-week):
- A/B prefetch policy: baseline prefetch (N=3 prefixes) vs aggressive (N=10) on 5% of traffic; measure prefetch-efficacy and cost delta. Owner: Marcus. Start: 2026-02-10.
- Probe cadence change: synthetic probe every 30s vs 90s in canary region to measure detection latency. Owner: Aisha.

Runbook readiness checklist before rollout (must pass all):
- [ ] Dashboard micro-tiles implemented and visible to oncall
- [ ] Metric derivations documented in Confluence (CONFLUENCE-OBS-1234)
- [ ] Sampling rules deployed to trace-agent and validated on staging
- [ ] Synthetic probes updated and baseline established (3 days)
- [ ] Pre-roll A/B experiment queued and monitoring hooks created

Cost guardrails (notes):
- Trace retention: keep full traces for 7 days for high-severity, 30 days aggregated indices only.
- Sampling lowered automatically if monthly trace spend exceeds budget (alert to infra-finance).
- Consider compact encoding for span attributes (store booleans as flags).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we add a "prefetch-hit-streak" histogram (consecutive hit rate) per tenant? (Pros: captures transient warming; Cons: increases cardinality)
- Decide canonical name for "kv-warmth-index" (maybe kv-warmth-v1).
- Who owns tenant-level baselines? (suggest SRE-allocations team)
- Automation: can prefetch-efficacy trigger autoscaling policy? sketch needed.

Notes-to-self / rough action items:
- Make a small PR to normalize span names (append model_variant) — PRIYA to own.
- Wire a small widget into oncall mobile home screen for prefetch-efficacy critical alerts.
- Draft short training doc for support engineers: 1-page cheat sheet + 3 example traces.

References and links:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-OBS-1234 (signal glossary)
- Jira: JIRA-OBS-789 (dashboard micro-tiles epic)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-playbooks/pull/42
- Slack thread: #obs-kv-prefetch (see 2026-01-08 pinned message)

Endnotes: this is intentionally compact — save the long-form instrumentation cookbook for the Confluence page. Keep this doc as the short route for oncall and PMs.
